title: A Unified Quantum Interferometric Framework for Interaction-Free Measurement and Delayed-Choice Experiments
authors: Hitesh Awasthi, Sandeep Mishra, Anirban Pathak
abstract: A theoretical unified interferometric framework is developed for interaction-free measurement (IFM) and delayed-choice (DC) experiments. The proposed model leads to a quantum circuit based architecture in which an ancillary qubit coherently controls the interaction between a photon and a bomb, allowing the system to evolve in a superposition of interaction and non-interaction regimes. The ancillary control qubit serves as a quantum switch that continuously interpolates between IFM and DC behavior, revealing a common operational origin for both phenomena. We demonstrate that both the phenomena can be realized within this framework through controlled quantum-gate operations. The analysis shows that the framework enables a continuous transition between the particle-like and wave-like behavior in DC setup. The framework is shown to be consistent with standard quantum mechanics, preserving unitary evolution, quantum superposition and the measurement postulate.
summary: The paper introduces a novel, unified interferometric framework to mathematically connect Interaction-Free Measurement and Delayed-Choice experiments. By modeling the system using an extended MZI circuit involving four qubits, it shows that both phenomena arise from the same underlying quantum evolution. This provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding wave-particle duality and counterfactual information extraction simultaneously.
main_problem: The paper develops a theoretical framework to unify two distinct quantum phenomena: Interaction-Free Measurement (IFM) and Delayed-Choice (DC) experiments.
main_result: It demonstrates that IFM and DC behavior share a common operational origin, emerging from the same underlying interferometric structure controlled by ancillary qubits.
method: The authors use a quantum circuit representation based on an extended Mach-Zehnder Interferometer involving four qubits to model the coherent evolution of the system.

main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that absorbed photons do not participate in further unitary evolution, regardless of the BS2 presence.
